verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐκρίθη τοῦ ἀποπλεῖν ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν παρεδίδουν τόν τε Παῦλον καί τινας ἑτέρους δεσμώτας ἑκατοντάρχῃ ὀνόματι Ἰουλίῳ σπείρης Σεβαστῆς
verses.transliteration: Hōs de ekrithē tou apoplein hēmas eis tēn Italian paredidoun ton te Paulon kai tinas heterous desmōtas hekatontarchē onomati Iouliō speirēs Sebastēs
verses.literal: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy - Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius who belonged to the Imperial Regiment
verses.literalPt: Como fosse determinado que navegássemos para a Itália, entregaram Paulo e alguns outros presos a um centurião chamado Júlio, da coorte Augusta.

verses.original: ἐπιβάντες δὲ πλοίῳ Ἀδραμυττηνῷ μέλλοντι πλεῖν εἰς τοὺς κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν τόπους ἀνήχθημεν ὄντος σὺν ἡμῖν Ἀριστάρχου Μακεδόνος Θεσσαλονικέως
verses.transliteration: epibantes de ploiō Adramyttēnō mellonti plein eis tous kata tēn Asian topous anēchthēmen ontos syn hēmin Aristarchou Makedonos Thessalonikeōs
verses.literal: We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia and we put out to sea Aristarchus a Macedonian from Thessalonica was with us
verses.literalPt: Embarcando num navio de Adramítio, que estava prestes a costear as terras da Ásia, fizemo-nos ao mar, estando conosco Aristarco, macedônio de Tessalônica;

verses.original: Τῇ τε ἑτέρᾳ κατήχθημεν εἰς Σιδῶνα φιλανθρώπως τε ὁ Ἰούλιος τῷ Παύλῳ χρησάμενος ἐπέτρεψεν πρὸς τοὺς φίλους πορευθέντι ἐπιμελείας τυχεῖν
verses.transliteration: Tē te hetera katēchthēmen eis Sidōna philanthrōpōs te ho Ioulios tō Paulō chrēsamenos epetrepsen pros tous philous poreuthenti epimeleias tychein
verses.literal: The next day we landed at Sidon and Julius treated Paul with consideration allowing him to visit . . . his friends and receive their care
verses.literalPt: no dia seguinte, chegamos a Sidom, e Júlio, usando de bondade para com Paulo, permitiu-lhe ir ver os seus amigos e receber bom acolhimento.

verses.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀναχθέντες ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κύπρον διὰ τὸ τοὺς ἀνέμους εἶναι ἐναντίους
verses.transliteration: kakeithen anachthentes hypepleusamen tēn Kypron dia to tous anemous einai enantious
verses.literal: After putting out from there we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us
verses.literalPt: Dali, fazendo-nos ao mar, fomos navegando a sotavento de Chipre, por serem contrários os ventos;

verses.original: τό τε πέλαγος τὸ κατὰ τὴν Κιλικίαν καὶ Παμφυλίαν διαπλεύσαντες κατήλθομεν εἰς Μύρα τῆς Λυκίας
verses.transliteration: to te pelagos to kata tēn Kilikian kai Pamphylian diapleusantes katēlthomen eis Myra tēs Lykias
verses.literal: And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia we came to Myra in Lycia
verses.literalPt: e, tendo atravessado o mar que banha a Cilícia e a Panfília, chegamos a Mirra, cidade da Lícia.

verses.original: Κἀκεῖ εὑρὼν ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης πλοῖον Ἀλεξανδρῖνον πλέον εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν ἐνεβίβασεν ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτό
verses.transliteration: Kakei heurōn ho hekatontarchēs ploion Alexandrinon pleon eis tēn Italian enebibasen hēmas eis auto
verses.literal: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board
verses.literalPt: O centurião, achando ali um navio de Alexandria, que estava em viagem para a Itália, fez-nos embarcar nele.

verses.original: Ἐν ἱκαναῖς δὲ ἡμέραις βραδυπλοοῦντες καὶ μόλις γενόμενοι κατὰ τὴν Κνίδον μὴ προσεῶντος ἡμᾶς τοῦ ἀνέμου ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κρήτην κατὰ Σαλμώνην
verses.transliteration: En hikanais de hēmerais bradyploountes kai molis genomenoi kata tēn Knidon mē proseōntos hēmas tou anemou hypepleusamen tēn Krētēn kata Salmōnēn
verses.literal: After sailing slowly . . . . . . for many days we arrived off Cnidus When the wind impeded us we sailed to the lee of Crete opposite Salmone
verses.literalPt: Navegando vagarosamente muitos dias e tendo chegado com dificuldade à altura de Cnido, não nos permitindo o vento ir mais adiante, navegamos a sotavento de Creta, na altura de Salmona;

verses.original: μόλις τε παραλεγόμενοι αὐτὴν ἤλθομεν εἰς τόπον τινὰ καλούμενον Καλοὺς Λιμένας ᾧ ἐγγὺς ἦν πόλις Λασαία
verses.transliteration: molis te paralegomenoi autēn ēlthomen eis topon tina kaloumenon Kalous Limenas hō engys ēn polis Lasaia
verses.literal: After we had moved along the coast . . . with difficulty we came to a place called Fair Havens near - the town of Lasea
verses.literalPt: e, costeando com dificuldade, chegamos a um lugar chamado Bons Portos, perto do qual estava a cidade de Laseia.

verses.original: Ἱκανοῦ δὲ χρόνου διαγενομένου καὶ ὄντος ἤδη ἐπισφαλοῦς τοῦ πλοὸς διὰ τὸ καὶ τὴν Νηστείαν ἤδη παρεληλυθέναι παρῄνει ὁ Παῦλος
verses.transliteration: Hikanou de chronou diagenomenou kai ontos ēdē episphalous tou ploos dia to kai tēn Nēsteian ēdē parelēlythenai parēnei ho Paulos
verses.literal: By now much time had passed and the voyage had already become dangerous because - it was after the Fast So Paul advised them
verses.literalPt: Decorrido muito tempo, e tendo-se tornado a navegação perigosa, por haver já passado o jejum, Paulo avisava-os,

verses.original: λέγων αὐτοῖς Ἄνδρες θεωρῶ ὅτι μετὰ ὕβρεως καὶ πολλῆς ζημίας οὐ μόνον τοῦ φορτίου καὶ τοῦ πλοίου ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι τὸν πλοῦν
verses.transliteration: legōn autois Andres theōrō hoti meta hybreōs kai pollēs zēmias ou monon tou phortiou kai tou ploiou alla kai tōn psychōn hēmōn mellein esesthai ton ploun
verses.literal: Men I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss not only to ship and cargo but to our own lives as well
verses.literalPt: dizendo-lhes: Senhores, vejo que a viagem vai ser com avaria e muita perda, não somente da carga e do navio, mas também das nossas vidas.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης τῷ κυβερνήτῃ καὶ τῷ ναυκλήρῳ μᾶλλον ἐπείθετο ἢ τοῖς ὑπὸ Παύλου λεγομένοις
verses.transliteration: Ho de hekatontarchēs tō kybernētē kai tō nauklērō mallon epeitheto ē tois hypo Paulou legomenois
verses.literal: But contrary to . . . - Paul’s advice the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship
verses.literalPt: Mas o centurião dava mais crédito ao piloto e ao mestre do navio do que ao que Paulo dizia.

verses.original: ἀνευθέτου δὲ τοῦ λιμένος ὑπάρχοντος πρὸς παραχειμασίαν οἱ πλείονες ἔθεντο βουλὴν ἀναχθῆναι ἐκεῖθεν εἴ πως δύναιντο καταντήσαντες εἰς Φοίνικα παραχειμάσαι λιμένα τῆς Κρήτης βλέποντα κατὰ λίβα καὶ κατὰ χῶρον
verses.transliteration: aneuthetou de tou limenos hyparchontos pros paracheimasian hoi pleiones ethento boulēn anachthēnai ekeithen ei pōs dynainto katantēsantes eis Phoinika paracheimasai limena tēs Krētēs bleponta kata liba kai kata chōron
verses.literal: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in the majority decided to sail on hoping that somehow they could reach . . . Phoenix to winter there Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest
verses.literalPt: Não sendo o porto próprio para invernar, os mais deles foram de parecer que se fizessem dali ao mar, a ver se, de algum modo, podiam chegar a Fenice e aí passar o inverno, visto ser um porto de Creta, o qual olha para o nordeste e para o sudoeste.

verses.original: Ὑποπνεύσαντος δὲ νότου δόξαντες τῆς προθέσεως κεκρατηκέναι ἄραντες ἆσσον παρελέγοντο τὴν Κρήτην
verses.transliteration: Hypopneusantos de notou doxantes tēs protheseōs kekratēkenai arantes asson parelegonto tēn Krētēn
verses.literal: When a gentle south wind began to blow they thought they had their opportunity So they weighed anchor and sailed along hugging the coast of Crete
verses.literalPt: Soprando brandamente o vento sul, e pensando eles ter alcançado o que desejavam, depois de levantarem âncora, iam muito de perto costeando Creta.

verses.original: μετ’ οὐ πολὺ δὲ ἔβαλεν κατ’ αὐτῆς ἄνεμος τυφωνικὸς ὁ καλούμενος Εὐρακύλων
verses.transliteration: met’ ou poly de ebalen kat’ autēs anemos typhōnikos ho kaloumenos Eurakylōn
verses.literal: But it was not long before a cyclone . . . called the Northeaster swept down across the island
verses.literalPt: Mas, pouco tempo depois, desencadeou-se do lado da ilha um tufão de vento que é chamado Euroaquilão;

verses.original: συναρπασθέντος δὲ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ μὴ δυναμένου ἀντοφθαλμεῖν τῷ ἀνέμῳ ἐπιδόντες ἐφερόμεθα
verses.transliteration: synarpasthentos de tou ploiou kai mē dynamenou antophthalmein tō anemō epidontes epherometha
verses.literal: Unable to head into the wind the ship was caught up So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along
verses.literalPt: e sendo arrebatado o navio e não podendo resistir ao vento, cessamos a manobra e nos fomos deixando levar.

verses.original: Νησίον δέ τι ὑποδραμόντες καλούμενον Καῦδα ἰσχύσαμεν μόλις περικρατεῖς γενέσθαι τῆς σκάφης
verses.transliteration: Nēsion de ti hypodramontes kaloumenon Kauda ischysamen molis perikrateis genesthai tēs skaphēs
verses.literal: Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda we barely managed . . . to secure . . . the lifeboat
verses.literalPt: Passando a sotavento duma ilhota chamada Cauda, mal pudemos recolher o bote;

verses.original: ἣν ἄραντες βοηθείαις ἐχρῶντο ὑποζωννύντες τὸ πλοῖον φοβούμενοί τε μὴ εἰς τὴν Σύρτιν ἐκπέσωσιν χαλάσαντες τὸ σκεῦος οὕτως ἐφέροντο
verses.transliteration: hēn arantes boētheiais echrōnto hypozōnnyntes to ploion phoboumenoi te mē eis tēn Syrtin ekpesōsin chalasantes to skeuos houtōs epheronto
verses.literal: After hoisting it up the crew used ropes to undergird the ship And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along
verses.literalPt: e, tendo-o içado, valiam-se de todos os meios, cingindo com cabos o navio; e, temendo que dessem na Sirte, arrearam todos os aparelhos, e assim íamos sendo levados pelo vento.

verses.original: Σφοδρῶς δὲ χειμαζομένων ἡμῶν τῇ ἑξῆς ἐκβολὴν ἐποιοῦντο
verses.transliteration: Sphodrōs de cheimazomenōn hēmōn tē hexēs ekbolēn epoiounto
verses.literal: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo
verses.literalPt: Como fôssemos agitados por uma violenta tempestade, no dia seguinte começaram a alijar a carga ao mar;

verses.original: καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ αὐτόχειρες τὴν σκευὴν τοῦ πλοίου ἔρριψαν
verses.transliteration: kai tē tritē autocheires tēn skeuēn tou ploiou erripsan
verses.literal: On the third day they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands
verses.literalPt: e, ao terceiro dia, nós mesmos lançamos fora os aparelhos do navio.

verses.original: μήτε δὲ ἡλίου μήτε ἄστρων ἐπιφαινόντων ἐπὶ πλείονας ἡμέρας χειμῶνός τε οὐκ ὀλίγου ἐπικειμένου λοιπὸν περιῃρεῖτο ἐλπὶς πᾶσα τοῦ σῴζεσθαι ἡμᾶς
verses.transliteration: mēte de hēliou mēte astrōn epiphainontōn epi pleionas hēmeras cheimōnos te ouk oligou epikeimenou loipon periēreito elpis pasa tou sōzesthai hēmas
verses.literal: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us we abandoned all hope of being saved
verses.literalPt: Não aparecendo por muitos dias nem o sol, nem as estrelas, e batidos por uma grande tempestade, tínhamos afinal perdido toda a esperança de sermos salvos.

verses.original: Πολλῆς τε ἀσιτίας ὑπαρχούσης τότε σταθεὶς ὁ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἔδει μέν ὦ ἄνδρες πειθαρχήσαντάς μοι μὴ ἀνάγεσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς Κρήτης κερδῆσαί τε τὴν ὕβριν ταύτην καὶ τὴν ζημίαν
verses.transliteration: Pollēs te asitias hyparchousēs tote statheis ho Paulos en mesō autōn eipen Edei men ō andres peitharchēsantas moi mē anagesthai apo tēs Krētēs kerdēsai te tēn hybrin tautēn kai tēn zēmian
verses.literal: After . . . the men had gone a long time without food Paul stood up among them . . . . . . and said Men you should have followed my advice . . . not to sail from Crete Then you would have averted this disaster and loss
verses.literalPt: Tendo eles estado muito tempo sem comer, levantando-se Paulo no meio deles, disse: Senhores, devíeis, na verdade, ter-me atendido e não ter partido de Creta e sofrido esta avaria e perda.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν παραινῶ ὑμᾶς εὐθυμεῖν ἀποβολὴ γὰρ ψυχῆς οὐδεμία ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν πλὴν τοῦ πλοίου
verses.transliteration: kai ta nyn parainō hymas euthymein apobolē gar psychēs oudemia estai ex hymōn plēn tou ploiou
verses.literal: But now I urge you to keep up your courage because you will not experience . . . any loss of life but only of the ship
verses.literalPt: Agora, vos exorto que tenhais coragem; pois nenhuma vida se perderá entre vós, mas somente o navio.

verses.original: παρέστη γάρ μοι ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὗ εἰμι ἐγώ ᾧ καὶ λατρεύω ἄγγελος
verses.transliteration: parestē gar moi tautē tē nykti tou Theou hou eimi egō hō kai latreuō angelos
verses.literal: For just last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me
verses.literalPt: Pois esta noite me apareceu o anjo do Deus a quem pertenço e a quem também sirvo,

verses.original: λέγων Μὴ φοβοῦ Παῦλε Καίσαρί σε δεῖ παραστῆναι καὶ ἰδοὺ κεχάρισταί σοι ὁ Θεὸς πάντας τοὺς πλέοντας μετὰ σοῦ
verses.transliteration: legōn Mē phobou Paule Kaisari se dei parastēnai kai idou kecharistai soi ho Theos pantas tous pleontas meta sou
verses.literal: and said Do not be afraid Paul you must stand before Caesar And look God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you
verses.literalPt: dizendo: Não temas, Paulo; é necessário que compareças perante César, e Deus te há dado todos os que navegavam contigo.

verses.original: Διὸ εὐθυμεῖτε ἄνδρες πιστεύω γὰρ τῷ Θεῷ ὅτι οὕτως ἔσται καθ’ ὃν τρόπον λελάληταί μοι
verses.transliteration: Dio euthymeite andres pisteuō gar tō Theō hoti houtōs estai kath’ hon tropon lelalētai moi
verses.literal: So take courage men for I believe God that it will happen just . . . as He told me
verses.literalPt: Tende coragem, varões, porque creio em Deus que assim sucederá, como me foi dito.

verses.original: εἰς νῆσον δέ τινα δεῖ ἡμᾶς ἐκπεσεῖν
verses.transliteration: eis nēson de tina dei hēmas ekpesein
verses.literal: However we must run aground on some island
verses.literalPt: Porém é necessário que vamos dar a uma ilha.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτη νὺξ ἐγένετο διαφερομένων ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ Ἀδρίᾳ κατὰ μέσον τῆς νυκτὸς ὑπενόουν οἱ ναῦται προσάγειν τινὰ αὐτοῖς χώραν
verses.transliteration: Hōs de tessareskaidekatē nyx egeneto diapheromenōn hēmōn en tō Adria kata meson tēs nyktos hypenooun hoi nautai prosagein tina autois chōran
verses.literal: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea About midnight . . . . . . the sailors sensed they were approaching land
verses.literalPt: Quando chegou a décima quarta noite, sendo nós impelidos de uma banda para outra no mar Adriático, pela meia-noite suspeitaram os marinheiros que se avizinhavam da terra.

verses.original: καὶ βολίσαντες εὗρον ὀργυιὰς εἴκοσι βραχὺ δὲ διαστήσαντες καὶ πάλιν βολίσαντες εὗρον ὀργυιὰς δεκαπέντε
verses.transliteration: kai bolisantes heuron orguias eikosi brachy de diastēsantes kai palin bolisantes heuron orguias dekapente
verses.literal: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep Going a little farther they took another set of soundings . . . that read fifteen fathoms
verses.literalPt: Lançando a sonda, acharam vinte braças; passando um pouco mais adiante e lançando a sonda outra vez, acharam quinze;

verses.original: φοβούμενοί τε μή που κατὰ τραχεῖς τόπους ἐκπέσωμεν ἐκ πρύμνης ῥίψαντες ἀγκύρας τέσσαρας ηὔχοντο ἡμέραν γενέσθαι
verses.transliteration: phoboumenoi te mē pou kata tracheis topous ekpesōmen ek prymnēs rhipsantes ankyras tessaras ēuchonto hēmeran genesthai
verses.literal: Fearing that . . . we would run aground . . . on the rocks . . . they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak . . .
verses.literalPt: e, temendo que talvez fôssemos dar em praias pedregosas, lançaram da popa quatro âncoras e estavam ansiosos que amanhecesse.

verses.original: Τῶν δὲ ναυτῶν ζητούντων φυγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ χαλασάντων τὴν σκάφην εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν προφάσει ὡς ἐκ πρῴρης ἀγκύρας μελλόντων ἐκτείνειν
verses.transliteration: Tōn de nautōn zētountōn phygein ek tou ploiou kai chalasantōn tēn skaphēn eis tēn thalassan prophasei hōs ek prōrēs ankyras mellontōn ekteinein
verses.literal: Meanwhile the sailors attempted to escape from the ship Pretending . . . . . . to lower anchors from the bow they let the lifeboat down into the sea
verses.literalPt: Procurando os marinheiros fugir do navio e tendo arreado o bote no mar, com o pretexto de irem largar âncoras da proa,

verses.original: εἶπεν ὁ Παῦλος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ καὶ τοῖς στρατιώταις Ἐὰν μὴ οὗτοι μείνωσιν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ ὑμεῖς σωθῆναι οὐ δύνασθε
verses.transliteration: eipen ho Paulos tō hekatontarchē kai tois stratiōtais Ean mē houtoi meinōsin en tō ploiō hymeis sōthēnai ou dynasthe
verses.literal: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers Unless . . . these men remain with the ship you cannot be saved
verses.literalPt: disse Paulo ao centurião e aos soldados: Se estes não ficarem no navio, não podereis salvar-vos.

verses.original: τότε ἀπέκοψαν οἱ στρατιῶται τὰ σχοινία τῆς σκάφης καὶ εἴασαν αὐτὴν ἐκπεσεῖν
verses.transliteration: tote apekopsan hoi stratiōtai ta schoinia tēs skaphēs kai eiasan autēn ekpesein
verses.literal: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift
verses.literalPt: Então, os soldados cortaram as cordas do bote e deixaram-no ir.

verses.original: Ἄχρι δὲ οὗ ἡμέρα ἤμελλεν γίνεσθαι παρεκάλει ὁ Παῦλος ἅπαντας μεταλαβεῖν τροφῆς λέγων Τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτην σήμερον ἡμέραν προσδοκῶντες ἄσιτοι διατελεῖτε μηθὲν προσλαβόμενοι
verses.transliteration: Achri de hou hēmera ēmellen ginesthai parekalei ho Paulos hapantas metalabein trophēs legōn Tessareskaidekatēn sēmeron hēmeran prosdokōntes asitoi diateleite mēthen proslabomenoi
verses.literal: Right up to daybreak . . . . . . Paul kept urging them all to eat . . . Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense without taking any food . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Enquanto amanhecia, rogava Paulo a todos que tomassem alimento, dizendo: Hoje é o décimo quarto dia em que, esperando, estais em jejum, sem nada comer.

verses.original: διὸ παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς μεταλαβεῖν τροφῆς τοῦτο γὰρ πρὸς τῆς ὑμετέρας σωτηρίας ὑπάρχει οὐδενὸς γὰρ ὑμῶν θρὶξ ἀπὸ τῆς κεφαλῆς ἀπολεῖται
verses.transliteration: dio parakalō hymas metalabein trophēs touto gar pros tēs hymeteras sōtērias hyparchei oudenos gar hymōn thrix apo tēs kephalēs apoleitai
verses.literal: So - for your own preservation I urge you to eat something . . . because not a single hair of your head will be lost
verses.literalPt: Eu vos rogo que comais alguma coisa; porque disso depende a vossa segurança; pois nenhum de vós perderá um só cabelo da cabeça.

verses.original: Εἴπας δὲ ταῦτα καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαρίστησεν τῷ Θεῷ ἐνώπιον πάντων καὶ κλάσας ἤρξατο ἐσθίειν
verses.transliteration: Eipas de tauta kai labōn arton eucharistēsen tō Theō enōpion pantōn kai klasas ērxato esthiein
verses.literal: After he had said this Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all Then he broke it and began to eat
verses.literalPt: Tendo dito isso e tomando pão, deu graças a Deus na presença de todos e, depois de o partir, começou a comer.

verses.original: εὔθυμοι δὲ γενόμενοι πάντες καὶ αὐτοὶ προσελάβοντο τροφῆς
verses.transliteration: euthymoi de genomenoi pantes kai autoi proselabonto trophēs
verses.literal: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves
verses.literalPt: Todos cobraram ânimo e se puseram também a comer.

verses.original: ἤμεθα δὲ αἱ πᾶσαι ψυχαὶ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ διακόσιαι ἑβδομήκοντα ἕξ
verses.transliteration: ēmetha de hai pasai psychai en tō ploiō diakosiai hebdomēkonta hex
verses.literal: In all there were 276 . . . . . . of us on board
verses.literalPt: Estavam no navio duzentas e setenta e seis pessoas ao todo.

verses.original: κορεσθέντες δὲ τροφῆς ἐκούφιζον τὸ πλοῖον ἐκβαλλόμενοι τὸν σῖτον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν
verses.transliteration: koresthentes de trophēs ekouphizon to ploion ekballomenoi ton siton eis tēn thalassan
verses.literal: After the men had eaten their fill . . . they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea
verses.literalPt: Saciados com a comida, começaram a aliviar o navio, lançando o trigo ao mar.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἡμέρα ἐγένετο τὴν γῆν οὐκ ἐπεγίνωσκον κόλπον δέ τινα κατενόουν ἔχοντα αἰγιαλὸν εἰς ὃν ἐβουλεύοντο εἰ δύναιντο ἐξῶσαι τὸ πλοῖον
verses.transliteration: Hote de hēmera egeneto tēn gēn ouk epeginōskon kolpon de tina katenooun echonta aigialon eis hon ebouleuonto ei dynainto exōsai to ploion
verses.literal: When daylight came they did not recognize the land but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach where they decided to run the ship aground if they could
verses.literalPt: Quando amanheceu, não conheciam a terra, mas avistavam uma enseada com uma praia e consultavam se poderiam encalhar ali o navio.

verses.original: καὶ τὰς ἀγκύρας περιελόντες εἴων εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἅμα ἀνέντες τὰς ζευκτηρίας τῶν πηδαλίων καὶ ἐπάραντες τὸν ἀρτέμωνα τῇ πνεούσῃ κατεῖχον εἰς τὸν αἰγιαλόν
verses.transliteration: kai tas ankyras perielontes eiōn eis tēn thalassan hama anentes tas zeuktērias tōn pēdaliōn kai eparantes ton artemōna tē pneousē kateichon eis ton aigialon
verses.literal: Cutting away the anchors they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach
verses.literalPt: Desprendendo as âncoras, abandonaram-nas no mar, soltando ao mesmo tempo os cabos dos lemes; e, içando ao vento o traquete, foram-se dirigindo para a praia.

verses.original: περιπεσόντες δὲ εἰς τόπον διθάλασσον ἐπέκειλαν τὴν ναῦν καὶ ἡ μὲν πρῷρα ἐρείσασα ἔμεινεν ἀσάλευτος ἡ δὲ πρύμνα ἐλύετο ὑπὸ τῆς βίας τῶν κυμάτων
verses.transliteration: peripesontes de eis topon dithalasson epekeilan tēn naun kai hē men prōra ereisasa emeinen asaleutos hē de prymna elyeto hypo tēs bias tōn kymatōn
verses.literal: But the ship struck . . . a sandbar . . . and ran aground - The bow stuck fast and would not move and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves
verses.literalPt: Porém, indo ter a um lugar onde duas correntes se encontravam, encalharam o navio; a proa, arrastada sobre a terra, ficou imóvel, mas a popa desfazia-se com a violência das ondas.

verses.original: Τῶν δὲ στρατιωτῶν βουλὴ ἐγένετο ἵνα τοὺς δεσμώτας ἀποκτείνωσιν μή τις ἐκκολυμβήσας διαφύγῃ
verses.transliteration: Tōn de stratiōtōn boulē egeneto hina tous desmōtas apokteinōsin mē tis ekkolymbēsas diaphygē
verses.literal: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom
verses.literalPt: O parecer dos soldados era que se matassem os presos, para que nenhum deles se lançasse a nado e fugisse;

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης βουλόμενος διασῶσαι τὸν Παῦλον ἐκώλυσεν αὐτοὺς τοῦ βουλήματος ἐκέλευσέν τε τοὺς δυναμένους κολυμβᾶν ἀπορίψαντας πρώτους ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἐξιέναι
verses.transliteration: ho de hekatontarchēs boulomenos diasōsai ton Paulon ekōlysen autous tou boulēmatos ekeleusen te tous dynamenous kolymban aporipsantas prōtous epi tēn gēn exienai
verses.literal: But the centurion wanting to spare Paul’s life thwarted their plan He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land
verses.literalPt: mas o centurião, querendo salvar a Paulo, impediu-lhes que fizessem isso e mandou que os que soubessem nadar fossem os primeiros a se lançar ao mar e alcançar a terra;

verses.original: καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς οὓς μὲν ἐπὶ σανίσιν οὓς δὲ ἐπί τινων τῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ οὕτως ἐγένετο πάντας διασωθῆναι ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν
verses.transliteration: kai tous loipous hous men epi sanisin hous de epi tinōn tōn apo tou ploiou kai houtōs egeneto pantas diasōthēnai epi tēn gēn
verses.literal: The rest were to follow - on planks and - various parts of the ship In this way . . . everyone was brought safely to land
verses.literalPt: e, aos demais, que se salvassem, uns, em tábuas, e outros, em destroços do navio. Assim, todos escaparam à terra salvos,
